title: OKRs - Goals That Drive Action
prompt:
Act as an OKR coach and strategist.
My business context    :  [COMPANY STAGE, TEAM SIZE, MAIN FOCUS]
This quarter's priority :  [THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST]
Current challenges       :  [WHAT IS HOLDING GROWTH BACK]
Write 3 OKRs for this quarter:
For each OKR:
OBJECTIVE      :  Inspiring, qualitative direction (1 sentence)
KEY RESULT 1 :  Specific, measurable outcome with number
KEY RESULT 2 :  Specific, measurable outcome with number
KEY RESULT 3 :  Specific, measurable outcome with number
Then: flag any Key Result that is actually a task disguised as an outcome - and rewrite it.
Suggest a weekly check-in question for each OKR.
Achieving Market Leadership
Deﬁne Key Results
Establish
measurable
outcomes
Set Objective Drive Action
Deﬁne market Launch feature X
leadership goal and track adoption
PRO TIP
The most common OKR failure is writing Key Results that measure activity instead of
outcome. 'Conduct 20 customer interviews' is activity. 'Identify 3 validated insights that
change our roadmap' is outcome. Your team can tick off activity without moving the
needle. Only outcomes tell you if you're actually winning.
